attributes.readMe:
## Warehouse (Lo)

Three kinds of location on one card, on purpose: a building you own, a 3PL that holds your stock, and a **virtual dropship location** that holds nothing at all but exists so an order can be allocated somewhere. Treating them as one card is what keeps allocation logic in one place.

Bin-level granularity is optional. A spare-room operation has no bins and reports no utilisation, rather than a fake 0%.

Coordinates are stored as a plain latitude/longitude pair rather than a geo field, so the card stays usable in realms that do not carry the catalog's geo blocks.

**The pair now has a reader.** The isolated view mounts the catalog's shared Leaflet renderer (`@cardstack/catalog/components/map-render`) beside the address, and the app's Inventory tab mounts the same component over every warehouse at once. Before that the coordinates were populated on every instance and drawn by nothing — a field written and never read. The coordinate getter is `@cached`, because the renderer decides whether to rebuild its layers on an identity check and a fresh array each render would re-fit the map under the reader.

### Example

Three warehouses: the Bermondsey arch (owned, 92% full), Trafford (3PL), and WidgetCo Direct (virtual — its isolated view explains that stock is never counted there).

### Non-goals

No slotting or bin optimisation. Bins are recorded, not arranged; `pick-list` sorts a route from bin labels and says why that is a property of the labelling rather than a solver.
